content.one_sentence_role: Defines equivalence by one surjective isometry intertwining all algebra actions.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be a complex $C^*$-algebra, with no unit assumed, and let $\pi:A\to\mathcal B(H)$ and $\rho:A\to\mathcal B(K)$ be $*$-representations on complex Hilbert spaces. They are unitarily equivalent precisely when the following condition holds.
content.definition_explanation: There exists a surjective complex-linear isometry $U:H\to K$ such that $$U(\pi(a)x)=\rho(a)(Ux)\qquad\text{for every }a\in A\text{ and }x\in H.$$ Equivalently, $U\pi(a)=\rho(a)U$ for all $a$, or $\rho(a)=U\pi(a)U^{-1}$. The inverse exists because $U$ is onto as well as isometric. An abstract isomorphism of $H$ and $K$ without these intertwining equations is not the defined condition.
content.assumptions: Both representations have the same source algebra. Neither irreducibility, nonzero action, separability, nor finite dimension is required.
content.conclusion: One unitary from $H$ onto $K$ intertwines the two actions of every algebra element.
